arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Carter Phillips argued the asbestos litigation crisis remains acute.
He stated the crisis is more severe than at any prior time.
Mr. Salmons argued the opposing sides cannot recover for future cancer anxiety.
He claimed this anxiety is separate from their asbestosis disease.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Freeman Ayers and other workers sued Norfolk & Western Railway. They claimed asbestosis and fear of future cancer. The lower court allowed recovery for that anxiety. The railroad argues this expands liability beyond the statute's intent.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of emotional distress damages in workplace injury claims. It determines whether fear of future illness counts as a present injury. The outcome shapes compensation standards for industrial disease victims nationwide.
